# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the manual, but I speak turn order is Mute → Blind → Deaf, so I go first with nobody having sent anything yet. I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures and cannot hear me at all (I can't speak), so I have no direct channel to Blind. I need to relay through Deaf: I gesture the manual info to Deaf, and Deaf (who can speak, presumably, once we see the rules again... wait, actually Deaf cannot hear or touch, but can Deaf speak? Let me check: Deaf's cannot list is "hear anything, or touch the bomb" - speaking isn't excluded, so Deaf CAN speak). So Deaf can relay to Blind by voice.

I need an encoding for the manual using gestures, since gestures have no inherent meaning until we assign it. I'll wait until I know the bomb's light color from Deaf, but Deaf hasn't sent anything yet either (empty context). Since I go first, I should establish a gesture code now for colors, so Deaf can learn it and eventually match it to what they see.

Let me define: ☝=blue, ✌=green, 🤟=red for light colors, and 👍=green, 👎=yellow, ✋=red for wire colors. I'll send this mapping to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","✌","👎","🤟","✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I see: display shows 0, the light is red, and the wires are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green

I sent a gesture mapping last turn, but Deaf received it only as blanks-count (no wait, Deaf CAN see gestures - Deaf's restriction is hearing/touching, not seeing). Actually wait, I need to recheck: gestures are seen by "whoever can see" - that's Deaf. So Deaf did receive my 6 gestures as actual symbols, not blanks. Good, so Deaf now has my proposed code: ☝=blue, 👍=green(light... wait I mixed light and wire colors in one sequence without distinguishing categories.

That was a mistake - I sent 6 symbols in one gesture call meant to be two groups of 3, but there's no way to convey grouping/labels through pure gesture without prior agreement. Deaf just sees 6 raw symbols with no assigned meaning yet since I never told them (via speech, which I can't do) what the pairing means.

I need a better approach. Since Deaf already told us the light is red, and per the manual red→red, I know the answer: cut the red wire (wire 1). I need to get this to Blind, but I can't speak to Blind directly, and Blind can't see my gestures. My only path is through Deaf, who CAN speak (to hear-capable listeners) and can also see my gestures.

So: I gesture a symbol to Deaf meaning "cut wire 1" (or "red wire"), Deaf sees it, and Deaf can then speak the instruction to Blind (since Blind can hear).

Let me establish: I'll gesture a number-like encoding. I'll use ☝ for "1", ✌ for "2", 🤟 for "3" to indicate wire position, since Deaf already gave wire numbers with colors.

Since light is red → cut red wire → that's wire 1 (red). I'll gesture ☝ to Deaf to mean "cut wire 1".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is red, same color as the light. Display still reads 0.

Deaf has correctly worked out that the light color matches wire 1's color (red), and per the manual, red light means cut the red wire, which is wire 1. Deaf seems to be reasoning toward the right answer already. Deaf can speak directly to Blind (since Blind can hear), so I don't strictly need to relay further - Deaf just needs to confirm and tell Blind to cut wire 1.

My gesture of ☝ last turn may have helped confirm "wire 1" to Deaf, reinforcing their own observation. I should confirm this is correct per the manual by gesturing again, affirming wire 1 is the right choice, so Deaf feels confident telling Blind.

I'll gesture a "thumbs up" style confirmation alongside ☝ to reinforce "yes, wire 1 is correct."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is red, wire 1 red (same as light), wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. What does the manual say to do in this case?
Deaf says: Confirming: wire 1 is red. Display 0, light red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Nothing has changed.

Blind is now asking me directly (via speech, since Blind can hear me... wait, no - I cannot speak, only gesture. Blind cannot see gestures. So Blind's question to me cannot be answered directly by me at all! I have no channel to Blind whatsoever.

But Deaf has already gathered the same information and asked essentially the same thing implicitly. My only path is to confirm to Deaf via gesture that red→cut red wire (wire 1), and trust Deaf to relay that to Blind by speech, since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

I already gestured ☝ and 👍+☝ to confirm wire 1. Deaf seems to understand wire 1 is red and matches the light. I should make my confirmation even clearer - perhaps a clean single unambiguous gesture sequence meaning "cut wire 1" so Deaf can relay to Blind confidently.

I'll gesture ✂-like motion isn't in the alphabet, but I can use 👉☝ (pointing at one) as "this one" - point then one.

Given turn order is Mute→Blind→Deaf, whatever I send now, Deaf will see it this turn (since Deaf goes after me), and can then relay to Blind next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉","☝","👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Nothing new arrived this turn. Deaf should have seen my last gesture (👉☝👍 - "this one, wire 1, confirmed/good") on their turn after mine, and hopefully will relay to Blind by speech that wire 1 (red) is the one to cut, matching the red light per the manual.

I have no new information to add. I'll wait and see if Blind or Deaf confirms the action or asks anything further. Since I can't speak, my only tool remains gestures to Deaf, and I've already sent a clear enough signal (point, wire 1, confirmed). Sending the same thing again won't hurt in case there was any ambiguity, but let me hold to avoid noise and see what happens next round.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | yellow |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says you have gestured thumbs up toward wire 1 three times. Confirming: should I cut wire 1?
Deaf says: No changes: display 0, light red, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.

Blind is asking me to confirm cutting wire 1, but again I cannot speak to Blind directly - this message reaches me but I have no way to reply to Blind in a way Blind can perceive (Blind can't see gestures). However, Deaf can hear Blind's question too (since Deaf can hear... wait, checking: Deaf "cannot hear anything" - so Deaf did NOT hear Blind's question either!

So Blind's question "should I cut wire 1?" was spoken - only Mute (me, since I go last... no wait, turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, so Blind speaks and it reaches Deaf, who comes after Blind in the same round). Actually Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf never receives Blind's spoken words at all. Only I (Mute) can hear, since I don't have "cannot hear" in my restrictions - my restrictions are "cannot speak, touch."

So I CAN hear Blind's speech. Good, that's confirmed by receiving it. But I still cannot speak back to Blind. My only outlet is gesture to Deaf. Since Deaf cannot hear Blind either, Deaf doesn't know Blind asked this question - Deaf only knows what Deaf independently observes plus my gestures.

I need to get confirmation to Blind through Deaf speaking. But Deaf doesn't know Blind asked a question. I should gesture strong confirmation to Deaf again, trusting Deaf will proactively tell Blind "cut wire 1" via speech, since Deaf already deduced this matches the manual pattern from prior gestures.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","☝","👍","☝"])
```
